newsitem.title: USA: Brokaw, Jennings get Turner offers -- sources say.
newsitem.headline: Brokaw, Jennings get Turner offers -- sources say.

text.p: Ted Turner wants a network anchorman to become the "on air leader" of his Cable News Network and apparently has made offers to ABC's Peter Jennings and NBC's Tom Brokaw, broadcasting sources said on Wednesday.
Speaking after the New York Times reported that Turner made a $7 million offer to Brokaw to jump ship, the sources said Jennings also received a similar offer.
Both anchormen are currently renegotiating their contracts which expire later this year, but the sources said that while the men were no doubt flattered, it was doubtful that either would be tempted.
CBS anchorman Dan Rather has a contract that keeps him at his netowrk through 2000.
NBC is a unit of General Electric Co, ABC is a unit of Disney Co., CBS is a unit of Westinghouse Electric Co. and CNN is a unit of Time Warner Inc..

More than 40 million people a night watch the network evening news shows compared to a CNN viewership of about a million a day, industry sources said, adding that CNN has intense competition from two NBC cable channels and from an all-news station run by Fox.
A spokesman for Jennings had no comment while an NBC spokeswoman said Turner regularly offered network broadcasting stars about $7 million a year to join CNN.
She added that Brokaw told NBC affiliates in a speech on Monday that he looked forward to spending the rest of his career at NBC.
A spokesman for Turner said he had no comment on the offer to Brokaw and added, "this is the first I am hearing about Jennings." He had no comment on the ABC newsman as well.
The New York Times said Turner offered Brokaw, a longtime friend, a contract worth more than $7 million a year to become CNN's "on air leader."
Quoting two executives familiar with the negotiations, the newspaper said CNN would give Brokaw a nightly hour prime-time news programme plus several special programmes.

Brokaw is reportedly paid about $4 million a year and broadcasting sources said he is probably the lowest paid of the three network anchormen with Jennings reportedly receiving $7 million a year and Rather receiving about $5 million.
Don Hewitt, the executive producer of CBS's "60 Minutes" recently went on record offering Jennings a job if he jumps ship.
NBC's "Nightly News" has led rivals CBS and ABC in the ratings for 19 of the past 21 weeks, but has fallen behind ABC twice in the last three weeks.
